title: Vaudreuil to the minister of the Marine, cipher letter, Montréal, 13 Aug 1760, ANOM COL C11A 105 ff.147-152 (catalogue 1391)

documents.shelfmark: ANOM COL C11A 105 ff.147-152 (CABAC_PIAF_61062; LAC e000875753-58)

plaintext.source: No decipherment, clear copy or edition found (vetting 3 Nov 2026, web search 5 Nov 2026); ANOM COL F3 16 copy and the LAC C11A transcript reels not opened.

transcription.source: LAC microfilm images e000875753-58 (1125 px wide); the last group of every left-hand line is cut by the binding
transcription.notes: 2397 groups seen (81 of them partly), 27 more wholly lost in the gutter, 35 words in clear (not counted). ct.txt keeps the partly seen groups with '~' for the cut digits. Third pass 5 Nov: an interlinear line on f.150v moved to its caret and a spurious duplicate group removed.

system.summary: 700-entry table of numbered words, place and ship names, syllables and single letters (1757 Vaudreuil table), with names and titles left in clear and phonetic spelling.
system.sibling_key: The same 1757 table reads cat. 1388 (8 Apr 1759), 1389 (10 Apr 1759) and 1390 (16 Apr 1759) of C11A 104 in full; cat. 1392 (Trémais) uses another code. Sheet e001295272 of the same volume does not fit.
system.notes: Table in numerical order only on the sheet used (the alphabetical sheets e001295267/69 give the same entries by word).

conditions.human_role: Pasted the task brief; no other input.

solution.what: Catalogue entry and vetting record read; web searches (FR/EN) on the letter and its correspondents: no decipherment; key lead C11E 10 ff.285-290v.
Six letter images and ten key-volume images fetched from the LAC image server (curl -L; 503 on 28 Oct, working 5 Nov).
Numerical sheet e001295272 of the key volume tried on the ten commonest groups: nonsense.
Numerical sheet e001295274 tried: 642 de, 163 a, 144 pour, 430 les, 673 la, 594 ce, 547 que.
All 700 entries of sheet e001295274 transcribed from 16 enlarged cell montages (uncertain cells marked).
Letter transcribed from enlarged half-spread crops (2398 groups seen, 35 clear words).
First decode with the table as read: French at once; names Amherst, Murray, Bigot, Lévis, Ristigouche.
32 table cells corrected from context (long s read as f, l/t, c/e, b/h, homophones); inserted groups above lines added to the stream.
One group re-checked on the image (f.151r line 4, 383); historical consistency: Murray's circular, Restigouche, Lévis, Bigot, Amherst's junction at Montréal.
Coverage measured from the reading: 92.4% of all groups, 96.7% of the complete ones; 3.2% legible unread; 4.5% lost in the gutter.

Neighbouring records of C11A 105 (ff.136-146, 153-155) opened: clear letters of 7 and 13 Aug 1760 name the Machault, Bienfaisant and Marquis de Malauze, d'Angeac, La Giraudais, Villemont, the goélette l'Extravagante; none repeats the cipher letter.

Second pass with the corrected key and the images: 20 more groups read (devons, lorsque, se sera décidé, poste, coûteroit, Ontario, moindre, quarante mille ...); 25 gutter-cut groups restored from visible digits; measured 95.3% (96.3% with restored).

Sibling cipher letters of the same hand (cat. 1388-1390, 1392; C11A 104, 1759) tested with the same table: 1390 reads in full (354 groups), 1389 sample reads, 1388 same groups; 1392 uses a different code and does not read.
Siblings gave one new cell (452 fret) and no reading for the 16 unread places of 1391.
Siblings transcribed whole from the LAC images: cat. 1388 (3637 groups), 1389 (1225), 1390 (354); all decode as French with the same table; 1392 does not.
Five table cells settled from the sibling letters (301 trou, 133 oit, 367 crai, 195 vrai, 613 cas) plus 452 fret; 656 left open.

Third pass on the images: the interlinear line on f.150v belongs at a caret after 'de' (a duplicate 51 removed): 'ces derniers se lassent de notre extrême indigence, il ne faut rien moins que mes soins'; 'qui[n]ze', '[Lou]isbourg' and 'aie [don]né' settle three more places.

Alphabetical sheet e001295269 of the same volume (rotated, enlarged 5x) confirms cells 473 moyen, 152 ton, 671 bateau; cell 2 reads 'campagne' (compagnie is 102): override added. No further gap closes.

Reading read as French sentences against the English translation; every paragraph builds sentences, holes are scattered. Measured with tools/stats.py: 2328 of 2424 groups (96.0%) as written, 97.1% with 25 restored gutter-cut groups; 24 legible groups unread in 9 places, 47 lost in the gutter.

validation.notes: key found in the same volume and applied; not recovered from the ciphertext

texts.label: ANOM COL C11A 105 ff.147-152
texts.summary: Vaudreuil reports to the minister on the eve of the capitulation: three ships and troops bound for Restigouche under d'Angeac, the frigate Machault (La Giraudais) to run the British blockade, the lake Champlain and Ontario flotillas lost, no powder or food, Amherst, Murray and the British fleet converging on Montréal, Murray's circular letter against the paper money, and a request that the King be told the colony will fall only at the last extremity.

reading_review.by: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (a model reading, not a person), after the solving passes
reading_review.note: Read the French sentence by sentence against reading_en.md: all paragraphs of ff.147r-152r build coherent, idiomatic 1760 chancery French with a consistent argument (the ships bound for Restigouche and the Machault, the loss of the flotillas, the English landing and their treatment of the Canadians, no powder or food, Murray's circular against the paper money, the request to the minister). Holes are scattered (about one line in four, mostly the last group of left-hand lines lost in the binding) and none leaves a sentence unreadable. Not checked by a person; spellings are phonetic in the cipher and modernised only inside brackets.

outcome.notes: No control run: the key was found, not recovered from the ciphertext.
